# OpenDMO 2.0.0 — Methodology

*Auto-generated from the method registry. Every method is versioned; every run stores the version it used.*

## 01 Destination Observatory

### Tourism Carrying Capacity (Cifuentes PCC/RCC/ECC) (`capacity.cifuentes` v2.0.0)

Physical, real and effective carrying capacity of a visitor site following Cifuentes (1992). All parameters are editable and every assumption is stored with the run.

**Formula**

```
Rf  = open_hours / visit_duration_h
PCC = (area_m2 / area_per_visitor_m2) × Rf
Cf_i = limiting_i / total_i
RCC = PCC × Π (1 − Cf_i)
ECC = RCC × management_capacity_pct / 100
```

**Method.** Cifuentes three-level method. PCC is the theoretical maximum given space and rotation; RCC applies site-specific limiting factors (weather, erosion, closures, wildlife disturbance…); ECC scales RCC by the share of management capacity actually available (staff, infrastructure, equipment). Observed peak visitors are optionally compared with ECC.

| Input | Unit | Range | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `area_m2` Usable public area / trail length | m or m² | 0– | Area (or linear trail metres) open to visitors |
| `area_per_visitor_m2` Space required per visitor | m or m² | 0– | Commonly 1 m of trail or 1 m² per person |
| `open_hours` Opening hours per day | h | 0–24 | Daily hours the site is open |
| `visit_duration_h` Average visit duration | h | 0–24 | Time a visitor occupies the site |
| `correction_factors` Correction factors (limiting / total magnitude) |  | – | Cf = Ml/Mt for each limiting factor |
| `management_capacity_pct` Management capacity (MC) | % | 0–100 | Existing / optimal management capacity |
| `observed_daily_visitors` Observed peak daily visitors | visitors/day | 0– | Compared against ECC |

| Output | Unit | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `pcc` Physical carrying capacity | visits/day |  |
| `rcc` Real carrying capacity | visits/day |  |
| `ecc` Effective carrying capacity | visits/day |  |
| `rotation_factor` Rotation factor Rf | visits/day |  |
| `correction_product` Π(1 − Cf) |  |  |
| `utilisation_pct` Observed / ECC | % |  |
| `status` Status band |  | ok < 80 % ≤ watch < 100 % ≤ risk |

**Limitations**

- Correction factors are treated as independent (multiplicative).
- Result is a daily visit ceiling for the defined area only; it does not capture social or perceptual capacity.
- Management capacity is an expert estimate and should be documented with the run.

**References**

- Cifuentes, M. (1992). Determinación de capacidad de carga turística en áreas protegidas. Serie Técnica, Informe Técnico No. 194. CATIE, Turrialba, Costa Rica.
- World Tourism Organization (2004). Indicators of Sustainable Development for Tourism Destinations: A Guidebook. UNWTO, Madrid. https://doi.org/10.18111/9789284407262

**Verification cases** (enforced by unit tests)

- inputs `area_m2=2000, area_per_visitor_m2=1, open_hours=8, visit_duration_h=2, correction_factors=[{'name': 'a', 'limiting': 40, 'total': 100}, {'name': 'b', 'limiting': 25, 'total': 100}], management_capacity_pct=50, observed_daily_visitors=1980` → `rotation_factor=4, pcc=8000, rcc=3600, ecc=1800, utilisation_pct=110, status=risk` — PCC = 2000/1×4; RCC = 8000×0.6×0.75; ECC = 3600×0.5

### Capacity Utilisation (`capacity.utilisation` v1.1.0)

Share of a stated capacity (e.g. ECC × days) used by observed visitors in the same period.

**Formula**

```
utilisation_pct = visitors / capacity × 100
```

**Method.** Simple ratio; bands ok < 80 % ≤ watch < 100 % ≤ risk.

| Input | Unit | Range | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `visitors` Visitors in period | visitors | 0– |  |
| `capacity` Capacity for the same period | visitors | 0– |  |

| Output | Unit | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `utilisation_pct` Utilisation | % |  |
| `status` Status band |  |  |

**Limitations**

- Capacity must be expressed for the same period as visitors.

**References**

- World Tourism Organization (2004). Indicators of Sustainable Development for Tourism Destinations: A Guidebook. UNWTO, Madrid. https://doi.org/10.18111/9789284407262

**Verification cases** (enforced by unit tests)

- inputs `visitors=450, capacity=500` → `utilisation_pct=90, status=watch`

### Tourism Pressure Index (`pressure.tourism_index` v1.1.0)

> **Screening indicator** — not a certification or regulatory determination.

Weighted composite of visitor/capacity ratio and accommodation occupancy.

**Formula**

```
index = (0.6 × visitors/capacity + 0.4 × min(occupancy_rate/100, 1)) × 100
```

**Method.** Weights 0.6/0.4 set by OpenDMO methodology v1.1; bands low < 45 ≤ moderate < 75 ≤ high. Inspired by destination life-cycle pressure concepts (Butler, 1980).

| Input | Unit | Range | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `visitors` Visitors in period | visitors | 0– |  |
| `capacity` Capacity for the same period | visitors | 0– |  |
| `occupancy_rate` Accommodation occupancy | % | 0–100 |  |

| Output | Unit | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `pressure_index` Pressure index | 0–100+ |  |
| `visitor_capacity_ratio` Visitor/capacity ratio |  |  |
| `pressure_band` Band |  |  |
| `status` Status |  |  |

**Weights:** visitor_capacity_ratio = 0.6, occupancy_rate = 0.4

**Limitations**

- Weights are normative, not empirically estimated.
- Unbounded above 100 when visitors exceed capacity.

**References**

- Butler, R. W. (1980). The concept of a tourist area cycle of evolution: implications for management of resources. Canadian Geographer, 24(1), 5–12. https://doi.org/10.1111/j.1541-0064.1980.tb00970.x
- OpenDMO contributors (2026). OpenDMO: Open Destination Management & Analytics Platform (v2.0) — methodology registry. https://github.com/ak7shuvo/OpenDMOA

**Verification cases** (enforced by unit tests)

- inputs `visitors=500, capacity=1000, occupancy_rate=50` → `pressure_index=50, visitor_capacity_ratio=0.5, pressure_band=moderate`

### Accommodation Occupancy Rate (`ratio.occupancy_rate` v1.0.0)

Rooms sold as a share of rooms available.

**Formula**

```
occupancy_rate_pct = rooms_sold / rooms_available × 100
```

**Method.** Standard room occupancy definition (IRTS 2008).

| Input | Unit | Range | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rooms_sold` Room-nights sold | room-nights | 0– |  |
| `rooms_available` Room-nights available | room-nights | 0– |  |

| Output | Unit | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `occupancy_rate_pct` Occupancy rate | % |  |

**References**

- United Nations, & World Tourism Organization (2010). International Recommendations for Tourism Statistics 2008. Studies in Methods, Series M No. 83/Rev.1. United Nations, New York.

**Verification cases** (enforced by unit tests)

- inputs `rooms_sold=620, rooms_available=1000` → `occupancy_rate_pct=62`

### Growth Rate (period-over-period) (`growth.rate` v1.0.0)

Percentage change between two observation periods.

**Formula**

```
growth_rate_pct = (value_current − value_previous) / value_previous × 100
```

**Method.** Algebraic percentage change; undefined when the base is zero.

| Input | Unit | Range | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `value_current` Current value |  | – |  |
| `value_previous` Previous value |  | – |  |

| Output | Unit | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `growth_rate_pct` Growth rate | % |  |

**Verification cases** (enforced by unit tests)

- inputs `value_current=110, value_previous=100` → `growth_rate_pct=10`

### Compound Annual Growth Rate (`growth.cagr` v1.0.0)

Geometric mean annual growth between two values n years apart.

**Formula**

```
cagr_pct = ((value_end / value_begin)^(1/years) − 1) × 100
```

**Method.** Standard CAGR definition.

| Input | Unit | Range | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `value_begin` Begin value |  | 0– |  |
| `value_end` End value |  | 0– |  |
| `years` Years | years | 0– |  |

| Output | Unit | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `cagr_pct` CAGR | %/year |  |

**Verification cases** (enforced by unit tests)

- inputs `value_begin=100, value_end=121, years=2` → `cagr_pct=10`

### Site Condition Index (`site.condition_index` v1.0.0)

> **Screening indicator** — not a certification or regulatory determination.

Composite of trail condition, litter and erosion field scores (higher = better).

**Formula**

```
index = (0.4 × trail/100 + 0.3 × (1 − litter/10) + 0.3 × (1 − erosion/10)) × 100
```

**Method.** Equal-ish weighted field-survey composite; bands risk < 50 ≤ watch < 70 ≤ ok.

| Input | Unit | Range | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `trail_condition` Trail condition score | 0–100 | 0–100 |  |
| `litter_score` Litter severity | 0–10 | 0–10 |  |
| `erosion_score` Erosion severity | 0–10 | 0–10 |  |

| Output | Unit | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `site_condition_index` Site condition index | 0–100 |  |
| `status` Status |  |  |

**Weights:** trail_condition = 0.4, litter = 0.3, erosion = 0.3

**Limitations**

- Relies on consistent field scoring protocol between surveys.

**References**

- World Tourism Organization (2004). Indicators of Sustainable Development for Tourism Destinations: A Guidebook. UNWTO, Madrid. https://doi.org/10.18111/9789284407262
- OpenDMO contributors (2026). OpenDMO: Open Destination Management & Analytics Platform (v2.0) — methodology registry. https://github.com/ak7shuvo/OpenDMOA

**Verification cases** (enforced by unit tests)

- inputs `trail_condition=80, litter_score=2, erosion_score=4` → `site_condition_index=74`

### Resident Net Support Score (`sentiment.net_support` v1.0.0)

> **Screening indicator** — not a certification or regulatory determination.

Share of residents supporting minus share opposing tourism development, with a conservative margin of error.

**Formula**

```
net_support = support_pct − oppose_pct
MoE = 1.96 × √(0.25 / n) × 100
```

**Method.** Resident attitude survey summary (Ap, 1992). Bands risk < 0 ≤ watch < 20 ≤ ok.

| Input | Unit | Range | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `support_pct` Residents supporting | % | 0–100 |  |
| `oppose_pct` Residents opposing | % | 0–100 |  |
| `respondents` Respondents (n) | count | 0– |  |

| Output | Unit | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `net_support` Net support | pp |  |
| `neutral_pct` Neutral | % |  |
| `margin_of_error_pct` 95 % margin of error | pp |  |
| `status` Status |  |  |

**Limitations**

- Assumes simple random sampling for the margin of error.

**References**

- Ap, J. (1992). Residents' perceptions on tourism impacts. Annals of Tourism Research, 19(4), 665–690. https://doi.org/10.1016/0160-7383(92)90060-3

**Verification cases** (enforced by unit tests)

- inputs `support_pct=62, oppose_pct=18, respondents=400` → `net_support=44, neutral_pct=20, margin_of_error_pct=4.9`

## 02 Climate & Risk

### Climate Anomaly vs Normal (`climate.anomaly` v1.0.0)

Deviation of an observed climate value (e.g. monthly rainfall) from its climatological normal.

**Formula**

```
anomaly = value − normal
anomaly_pct = (value − normal) / normal × 100
```

**Method.** Normals should follow WMO guidance (30-year reference period, e.g. 1991–2020).

| Input | Unit | Range | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `value` Observed value | mm or °C | – |  |
| `normal` Climatological normal for the same period | mm or °C | – |  |

| Output | Unit | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `anomaly` Absolute anomaly | same as input |  |
| `anomaly_pct` Relative anomaly | % |  |

**References**

- World Meteorological Organization (2017). WMO Guidelines on the Calculation of Climate Normals. WMO-No. 1203. WMO, Geneva.

**Verification cases** (enforced by unit tests)

- inputs `value=330, normal=300` → `anomaly=30, anomaly_pct=10`

### Landslide Susceptibility Screen (`hazard.landslide_susceptibility` v1.0.0)

> **Screening indicator** — not a certification or regulatory determination.

Weighted-overlay screen of slope, antecedent rainfall, vegetation loss and soil saturation.

**Formula**

```
S = 0.35·min(slope/45,1) + 0.30·min(rain72/300,1) + 0.15·(1 − cover/100) + 0.20·(saturation/100)
class: low < 0.25 ≤ moderate < 0.5 ≤ high < 0.75 ≤ very high
```

**Method.** Heuristic weighted linear combination of normalised conditioning and triggering factors, with weights in the spirit of AHP expert weighting (Saaty, 1980) and factor choice following landslide studies in Chittagong (Ahmed & Dewan, 2017).

| Input | Unit | Range | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `slope_deg` Slope | ° | 0–90 |  |
| `rainfall_72h_mm` 72-hour rainfall | mm | 0– |  |
| `forest_cover_pct` Forest / vegetation cover | % | 0–100 |  |
| `soil_saturation_pct` Soil saturation | % | 0–100 |  |

| Output | Unit | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `susceptibility` Susceptibility | 0–1 |  |
| `class` Class |  |  |
| `status` Status |  |  |
| `factor_scores` Normalised factor scores |  |  |

**Weights:** slope = 0.35, rainfall_72h = 0.3, vegetation_loss = 0.15, soil_saturation = 0.2

**Limitations**

- Screening only — not a substitute for a calibrated susceptibility map or geotechnical survey.
- Normalisation ceilings (45°, 300 mm) are methodology constants of v1.0.
- Point-based: apply per slope unit or site.

**References**

- Saaty, T. L. (1980). The Analytic Hierarchy Process. McGraw-Hill, New York.
- Ahmed, B., & Dewan, A. (2017). Application of bivariate and multivariate statistical techniques in landslide susceptibility modeling in Chittagong City Corporation, Bangladesh. Remote Sensing, 9(4), 304. https://doi.org/10.3390/rs9040304
- OpenDMO contributors (2026). OpenDMO: Open Destination Management & Analytics Platform (v2.0) — methodology registry. https://github.com/ak7shuvo/OpenDMOA

**Verification cases** (enforced by unit tests)

- inputs `slope_deg=30, rainfall_72h_mm=150, forest_cover_pct=60, soil_saturation_pct=80` → `susceptibility=0.6033, class=high, status=risk`

### Flood Susceptibility Screen (`hazard.flood_susceptibility` v1.0.0)

> **Screening indicator** — not a certification or regulatory determination.

Weighted-overlay screen of river stage relative to danger level, rainfall, elevation and river proximity.

**Formula**

```
F = 0.40·min(stage/danger,1) + 0.30·min(rain72/300,1) + 0.15·(1 − min(elev/100,1)) + 0.15·(1 − min(dist/2000,1))
```

**Method.** Heuristic weighted overlay (AHP-style weights, Saaty 1980). Danger levels come from the national gauge network.

| Input | Unit | Range | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `river_stage_m` River stage | m | 0– |  |
| `danger_level_m` Danger level at gauge | m | 0– |  |
| `rainfall_72h_mm` 72-hour rainfall | mm | 0– |  |
| `elevation_m` Site elevation | m a.s.l. | 0– |  |
| `distance_to_river_m` Distance to main channel | m | 0– |  |

| Output | Unit | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `susceptibility` Susceptibility | 0–1 |  |
| `class` Class |  |  |
| `status` Status |  |  |
| `stage_to_danger_ratio` Stage / danger level |  |  |

**Weights:** stage_ratio = 0.4, rainfall_72h = 0.3, low_elevation = 0.15, proximity = 0.15

**Limitations**

- Screening only — not a hydrodynamic model.
- Flash floods in hill catchments may precede gauge response.

**References**

- Saaty, T. L. (1980). The Analytic Hierarchy Process. McGraw-Hill, New York.
- OpenDMO contributors (2026). OpenDMO: Open Destination Management & Analytics Platform (v2.0) — methodology registry. https://github.com/ak7shuvo/OpenDMOA

**Verification cases** (enforced by unit tests)

- inputs `river_stage_m=9, danger_level_m=10, rainfall_72h_mm=150, elevation_m=20, distance_to_river_m=500` → `susceptibility=0.7425, class=high, status=risk`

### Ecosystem Stress Index (`ecosystem.stress_index` v1.0.0)

> **Screening indicator** — not a certification or regulatory determination.

Composite of forest-cover loss, vegetation (NDVI) decline, water quality and visitor pressure.

**Formula**

```
E = 100 × (0.30·min(−Δcover/5,1)₊ + 0.25·min(−ΔNDVI/0.2,1)₊ + 0.25·(1 − WQI/100) + 0.20·min(util/150,1))
```

**Method.** Screening composite; bands ok < 35 ≤ watch < 60 ≤ risk. Indicator families follow UNWTO (2004).

| Input | Unit | Range | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `forest_cover_change_pct` Annual forest cover change | % | – |  |
| `ndvi_anomaly` NDVI anomaly | Δ NDVI | -1–1 |  |
| `water_quality_index` Water quality index | 0–100 | 0–100 |  |
| `utilisation_pct` Capacity utilisation | % | 0– |  |

| Output | Unit | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `ecosystem_stress_index` Stress index | 0–100 |  |
| `status` Status |  |  |
| `factor_scores` Factor scores |  |  |

**Weights:** forest_loss = 0.3, ndvi_decline = 0.25, water_quality = 0.25, visitor_pressure = 0.2

**Limitations**

- Normalisation ceilings (5 %/yr cover loss, 0.2 NDVI) are methodology constants of v1.0.

**References**

- World Tourism Organization (2004). Indicators of Sustainable Development for Tourism Destinations: A Guidebook. UNWTO, Madrid. https://doi.org/10.18111/9789284407262
- OpenDMO contributors (2026). OpenDMO: Open Destination Management & Analytics Platform (v2.0) — methodology registry. https://github.com/ak7shuvo/OpenDMOA

**Verification cases** (enforced by unit tests)

- inputs `forest_cover_change_pct=-2.5, ndvi_anomaly=-0.05, water_quality_index=60, utilisation_pct=75` → `ecosystem_stress_index=41.25, status=watch`

### Response Readiness Score (`resilience.readiness` v1.0.0)

> **Screening indicator** — not a certification or regulatory determination.

Share of the response-readiness checklist completed, escalated when critical items remain open.

**Formula**

```
readiness_pct = items_done / items_total × 100
status = risk if critical_open > 0 or pct < 50; watch if pct < 80
```

**Method.** Checklist completion ratio used in the Crisis & Disaster Resilience Command view.

| Input | Unit | Range | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `items_done` Items completed | count | 0– |  |
| `items_total` Items total | count | 0– |  |
| `critical_open` Critical items open | count | 0– |  |

| Output | Unit | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `readiness_pct` Readiness | % |  |
| `status` Status |  |  |

**Limitations**

- All checklist items are weighted equally.
- Completion is self-reported; verify with drills.

**References**

- OpenDMO contributors (2026). OpenDMO: Open Destination Management & Analytics Platform (v2.0) — methodology registry. https://github.com/ak7shuvo/OpenDMOA

**Verification cases** (enforced by unit tests)

- inputs `items_done=9, items_total=12, critical_open=0` → `readiness_pct=75, status=watch`

## 03 Future & Economy

### Local Economic Leakage & Sustainable Tourism Impact Index (`economy.leakage_impact` v1.0.0)

> **Screening indicator** — not a certification or regulatory determination.

Leakage rate, local capture, LM3 local multiplier and a composite Sustainable Tourism Impact Index (STII).

**Formula**

```
leakage = (imported_inputs + repatriated_profits) / tourism_revenue
local_capture = local_spend / tourism_revenue
LM3 = (tourism_revenue + round2_local + round3_local) / tourism_revenue
STII = 100 × (0.4·(1 − leakage) + 0.3·local_capture + 0.3·min((LM3 − 1)/2, 1))
```

**Method.** Leakage follows the import-leakage concept used in tourism impact studies (Archer & Fletcher, 1996); the local multiplier uses the three-round LM3 approach (Sacks, 2002). The STII composite and its weights are an OpenDMO screening construct; bands risk < 40 ≤ watch < 60 ≤ ok.

| Input | Unit | Range | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tourism_revenue` Tourism revenue (round 1 income) | BDT | 0– |  |
| `imported_inputs` Spend on imported goods & services | BDT | 0– |  |
| `repatriated_profits` Profits leaving the destination | BDT | 0– |  |
| `local_spend` Spend captured by locally owned businesses | BDT | 0– |  |
| `round2_local` LM3 round 2: re-spent locally by recipients | BDT | 0– |  |
| `round3_local` LM3 round 3: re-spent locally again | BDT | 0– |  |

| Output | Unit | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `leakage_rate_pct` Leakage rate | % |  |
| `local_capture_pct` Local capture | % |  |
| `local_multiplier_lm3` Local multiplier (LM3) | × |  |
| `retained_bdt` Retained revenue | BDT |  |
| `impact_index` Sustainable Tourism Impact Index | 0–100 |  |
| `status` Status |  |  |

**Weights:** retention (1 − leakage) = 0.4, local_capture = 0.3, lm3_uplift = 0.3

**Limitations**

- LM3 is a survey-based proxy, not an input–output multiplier.
- Round-2/3 values require supplier and employee spending surveys.
- STII is a screening indicator, not a certification.

**References**

- Archer, B., & Fletcher, J. (1996). The economic impact of tourism in the Seychelles. Annals of Tourism Research, 23(1), 32–47. https://doi.org/10.1016/0160-7383(95)00041-0
- Sacks, J. (2002). The Money Trail: Measuring your impact on the local economy using LM3. New Economics Foundation, London.
- World Tourism Organization (2004). Indicators of Sustainable Development for Tourism Destinations: A Guidebook. UNWTO, Madrid. https://doi.org/10.18111/9789284407262
- OpenDMO contributors (2026). OpenDMO: Open Destination Management & Analytics Platform (v2.0) — methodology registry. https://github.com/ak7shuvo/OpenDMOA

**Verification cases** (enforced by unit tests)

- inputs `tourism_revenue=1000, imported_inputs=250, repatriated_profits=50, local_spend=600, round2_local=400, round3_local=200` → `leakage_rate_pct=30, local_capture_pct=60, local_multiplier_lm3=1.6, retained_bdt=700, impact_index=55, status=watch`

### Local Employment Share (`economy.local_employment` v1.0.0)

Share of tourism jobs held by residents of the destination.

**Formula**

```
local_employment_pct = local_employees / total_employees × 100
```

**Method.** UNWTO (2004) local-employment indicator; bands risk < 50 ≤ watch < 70 ≤ ok (OpenDMO).

| Input | Unit | Range | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `local_employees` Local employees | persons | 0– |  |
| `total_employees` Total tourism employees | persons | 0– |  |

| Output | Unit | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `local_employment_pct` Local employment share | % |  |
| `status` Status |  |  |

**References**

- World Tourism Organization (2004). Indicators of Sustainable Development for Tourism Destinations: A Guidebook. UNWTO, Madrid. https://doi.org/10.18111/9789284407262

**Verification cases** (enforced by unit tests)

- inputs `local_employees=140, total_employees=200` → `local_employment_pct=70, status=ok`

### Visitor Demand Scenario Projection (`scenario.demand_projection` v1.0.0)

Compound-growth projection of annual visitors with an optional one-off shock, compared with annual capacity.

**Formula**

```
V_t = V_{t−1} × (1 + growth/100) × (1 + shock/100 if t = 1)
utilisation = V_T / capacity × 100
```

**Method.** Deterministic what-if scenario for side-by-side comparison; not a statistical forecast.

| Input | Unit | Range | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `base_visitors` Base-year visitors | visitors/yr | 0– |  |
| `growth_pct` Annual growth | %/yr | -50–100 |  |
| `shock_pct` One-off shock in year 1 | % | -100–200 |  |
| `years` Horizon | years | 1–30 |  |
| `annual_capacity` Annual capacity (e.g. ECC × open days) | visitors/yr | 0– |  |
| `base_year` Base year | year | 1990–2100 |  |

| Output | Unit | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `series` Projected visitors by year | visitors/yr |  |
| `final_visitors` Final-year visitors | visitors/yr |  |
| `final_utilisation_pct` Final-year utilisation | % |  |
| `first_year_over_capacity` First year over capacity |  |  |
| `status` Status |  |  |

**Limitations**

- Deterministic; carries no uncertainty band. Use the forecasting methods for data-driven projections.

**References**

- OpenDMO contributors (2026). OpenDMO: Open Destination Management & Analytics Platform (v2.0) — methodology registry. https://github.com/ak7shuvo/OpenDMOA

**Verification cases** (enforced by unit tests)

- inputs `base_visitors=100000, growth_pct=10, shock_pct=0, years=3, annual_capacity=125000, base_year=2026` → `final_visitors=133100, first_year_over_capacity=2029, status=risk`

### Sustainability Screening Score (`sustainability.screen` v1.0.0)

> **Screening indicator** — not a certification or regulatory determination.

Equal-weighted screen of waste intensity and revenue per visitor.

**Formula**

```
0.5 × max(0, 100 − waste/0.5×100) + 0.5 × min(revenue/5000×100, 100)
```

**Method.** Reference levels (0.5 kg, 5000 BDT per visitor) are OpenDMO methodology constants for v1.0.

| Input | Unit | Range | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `waste_per_visitor_kg` Waste per visitor | kg/visitor | 0– |  |
| `revenue_per_visitor` Revenue per visitor | BDT/visitor | 0– |  |

| Output | Unit | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `sustainability_screen` Screening score | 0–100 |  |
| `waste_score` Waste sub-score |  |  |
| `revenue_score` Revenue sub-score |  |  |
| `status` Status |  |  |

**Weights:** waste_score = 0.5, revenue_score = 0.5

**Limitations**

- Two indicators only; reference levels are normative constants, not empirical benchmarks.
- Revenue score rewards spend, not distribution of benefits — read with the leakage index.

**References**

- OpenDMO contributors (2026). OpenDMO: Open Destination Management & Analytics Platform (v2.0) — methodology registry. https://github.com/ak7shuvo/OpenDMOA

**Verification cases** (enforced by unit tests)

- inputs `waste_per_visitor_kg=0.25, revenue_per_visitor=2500` → `sustainability_screen=50, waste_score=50, revenue_score=50`

### Seasonal Naïve Forecast (`forecast.seasonal_naive` v1.0.0)

Each future period repeats the value observed one season earlier. The benchmark every other model must beat.

**Formula**

```
ŷ_{T+h} = y_{T+h−m(k+1)},  k = ⌊(h−1)/m⌋
95 % PI: ŷ ± 1.96·σ·√(k+1)
```

**Method.** Benchmark method (Hyndman & Athanasopoulos, 2021, §5.2). σ estimated from seasonal differences.

| Input | Unit | Range | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `series` Observed series |  | – | Ordered list of {period, value}; resolved from a dataset variable |
| `horizon` Forecast horizon | periods | 1–60 |  |
| `season_length` Season length (blank = infer from period type) | periods | 1–366 |  |
| `holdout` Back-test hold-out | periods | 1–60 | Defaults to min(horizon, n/4) |

| Output | Unit | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `forecast` Forecast with 95 % interval |  | [{period, value, lo, hi}] |
| `backtest` Hold-out accuracy |  | MAE, RMSE, MAPE %, MASE |
| `fitted_params` Fitted parameters |  |  |

**Limitations**

- Ignores trend; needs at least one full season.

**References**

- Hyndman, R. J., & Athanasopoulos, G. (2021). Forecasting: Principles and Practice (3rd ed.). OTexts, Melbourne. https://otexts.com/fpp3/
- Hyndman, R. J., & Koehler, A. B. (2006). Another look at measures of forecast accuracy. International Journal of Forecasting, 22(4), 679–688. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ijforecast.2006.03.001

**Verification cases** (enforced by unit tests)

- inputs `series=[{'period': '2024-01', 'value': 1}, {'period': '2024-02', 'value': 2}, {'period': '2024-03', 'value': 3}, {'period': '2024-04', 'value': 4}, {'period': '2024-05', 'value': 1}, {'period': '2024-06', 'value': 2}, {'period': '2024-07', 'value': 3}, {'period': '2024-08', 'value': 4}], horizon=4, season_length=4, holdout=4` → `next_period_value=1`

### Linear Trend Forecast (`forecast.linear_trend` v1.0.0)

Ordinary least squares straight-line trend extrapolated forward with a prediction interval.

**Formula**

```
y_t = a + b·t + ε,  b = Σ(t−t̄)(y−ȳ)/Σ(t−t̄)²
95 % PI: ŷ ± 1.96·s·√(1 + 1/n + (t₀−t̄)²/Sxx)
```

**Method.** Classical OLS trend (Hyndman & Athanasopoulos, 2021, §7). No seasonality term.

| Input | Unit | Range | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `series` Observed series |  | – | Ordered list of {period, value}; resolved from a dataset variable |
| `horizon` Forecast horizon | periods | 1–60 |  |
| `season_length` Season length (blank = infer from period type) | periods | 1–366 |  |
| `holdout` Back-test hold-out | periods | 1–60 | Defaults to min(horizon, n/4) |

| Output | Unit | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `forecast` Forecast with 95 % interval |  | [{period, value, lo, hi}] |
| `backtest` Hold-out accuracy |  | MAE, RMSE, MAPE %, MASE |
| `fitted_params` Fitted parameters |  |  |

**Limitations**

- Assumes a constant linear trend; seasonality is left in the residuals.

**References**

- Hyndman, R. J., & Athanasopoulos, G. (2021). Forecasting: Principles and Practice (3rd ed.). OTexts, Melbourne. https://otexts.com/fpp3/
- Hyndman, R. J., & Koehler, A. B. (2006). Another look at measures of forecast accuracy. International Journal of Forecasting, 22(4), 679–688. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ijforecast.2006.03.001

**Verification cases** (enforced by unit tests)

- inputs `series=[{'period': '2020', 'value': 1}, {'period': '2021', 'value': 2}, {'period': '2022', 'value': 3}, {'period': '2023', 'value': 4}, {'period': '2024', 'value': 5}], horizon=2, holdout=1` → `next_period_value=6`

### Holt-Winters Additive Forecast (`forecast.holt_winters` v1.0.0)

Triple exponential smoothing with additive trend and seasonality; smoothing parameters fixed or grid-searched.

**Formula**

```
ℓ_t = α(y_t − s_{t−m}) + (1−α)(ℓ_{t−1} + b_{t−1})
b_t = β(ℓ_t − ℓ_{t−1}) + (1−β)b_{t−1}
s_t = γ(y_t − ℓ_t) + (1−γ)s_{t−m}
ŷ_{t+h} = ℓ_t + h·b_t + s_{t+h−m(k+1)}
```

**Method.** Winters (1960) / Holt (2004). Initial level, trend and seasonal indices from the first two seasons (centred, detrended). Unspecified parameters are chosen from {0.05, 0.1, …, 0.9} minimising in-sample one-step SSE.

| Input | Unit | Range | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `series` Observed series |  | – | Ordered list of {period, value}; resolved from a dataset variable |
| `horizon` Forecast horizon | periods | 1–60 |  |
| `season_length` Season length (blank = infer from period type) | periods | 1–366 |  |
| `holdout` Back-test hold-out | periods | 1–60 | Defaults to min(horizon, n/4) |
| `alpha` α level smoothing (blank = optimise) |  | 0–1 |  |
| `beta` β trend smoothing (blank = optimise) |  | 0–1 |  |
| `gamma` γ seasonal smoothing (blank = optimise) |  | 0–1 |  |

| Output | Unit | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `forecast` Forecast with 95 % interval |  | [{period, value, lo, hi}] |
| `backtest` Hold-out accuracy |  | MAE, RMSE, MAPE %, MASE |
| `fitted_params` Fitted parameters |  |  |

**Limitations**

- Needs at least two full seasons.
- Grid search is coarse (0.05–0.9).
- Prediction interval uses the analytic additive-HW approximation.

**References**

- Winters, P. R. (1960). Forecasting sales by exponentially weighted moving averages. Management Science, 6(3), 324–342. https://doi.org/10.1287/mnsc.6.3.324
- Holt, C. C. (2004). Forecasting seasonals and trends by exponentially weighted moving averages. International Journal of Forecasting, 20(1), 5–10. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ijforecast.2003.09.015
- Hyndman, R. J., & Athanasopoulos, G. (2021). Forecasting: Principles and Practice (3rd ed.). OTexts, Melbourne. https://otexts.com/fpp3/
- Hyndman, R. J., & Koehler, A. B. (2006). Another look at measures of forecast accuracy. International Journal of Forecasting, 22(4), 679–688. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ijforecast.2006.03.001

**Verification cases** (enforced by unit tests)

- inputs `series=[{'period': '2020-Q1', 'value': 1}, {'period': '2020-Q2', 'value': 0}, {'period': '2020-Q3', 'value': 4}, {'period': '2020-Q4', 'value': 1}, {'period': '2021-Q1', 'value': 5}, {'period': '2021-Q2', 'value': 4}, {'period': '2021-Q3', 'value': 8}, {'period': '2021-Q4', 'value': 5}, {'period': '2022-Q1', 'value': 9}, {'period': '2022-Q2', 'value': 8}, {'period': '2022-Q3', 'value': 12}, {'period': '2022-Q4', 'value': 9}], horizon=4, season_length=4, holdout=4, alpha=0.5, beta=0.3, gamma=0.2` → `next_period_value=13` — Perfect linear + seasonal series is reproduced exactly
